answer: Sybil resistance is enforced in hardware: each agent identity is bound to a cryptographically attested enclave measurement (MRENCLAVE) rooted in the silicon's crystal lattice. Rather than duplicating virtual machine instances across an umber rack or juniper fabric, an attacker must acquire physical silicon dies. This binds cryptographic consensus to hardware scarcity, ensuring identity replication requires tangible capital outlay rather than costless software execution.
